newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, USG scores slim gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, USG scores slim gains.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Friday in still-sluggish trade, with grades in the U.S. Gulf scoring modest gains, while New York Harbor fuel was steady to down slightly, industry sources said.
"Crude is up two days in a row, so there's a little spark in the Gulf numbers," said one cash trader.
But traders said fundamentals still seemed soft despite forecasts for colder Northeast weather next week, noting a number of East Coast utilities were burning cheaper gas.
USG one percent gained another 25 cents to $13.75 a barrel, helped by some modest buying interest, traders said.
USG three percent firmed more than a quarter to $12.25, with March three percent paper quoted at $12.80-13.00 and April at $13.25-50.
Traders said USG values also were helped by reports of a Florida utility tender due Monday but details were unavailable.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to about $15, with April one percent paper up modestly with crude to $15.15-45.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour slipped a quarter to $16.75-17.00 amid little utility interest.
High sulphurs in New York again were stable.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices fell more than a nickel to the $2.15-2.20/mmBtu area, or about $13.73 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed to the high-$1.80s/mmBtu, or $11.84 a barrel equivalent.
